Theme

Latin word

parō

parō, parāre, parāvī, parātum

verb, first conjugation

get, procure, buy; get, acquire (often by buying); prepare, get ready

In this lexicon

  • buy

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim hortōs (Lewis & Short s.v. parō); Traupman 130

  • get

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Amic. 55: amīcōs nōn parāre; Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim hortōs (Lewis & Short)

  • prepare

    the recommended word · classical · Phaedr. 3.19.1–2: parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius; Traupman 31, 364

Examples

  • plūribus verbīs ad tē scrībam, cum plūs ōtī nactus erō

    I’ll write to you at more length when I get more free timeCic. Fam. 3.7.1

    In the entry for get

  • canis parturiēns cum rogāsset alteram ut fētum in ejus tuguriō dēpōneret, facile impetrāvit

    a dog about to have puppies asked another to let her lay her litter in her kennel, and easily got her wayPhaedr. 1.19.3–5

    In the entry for get

  • amīcōs nōn parāre, optimam et pulcherrimam vītae, ut ita dīcam, supellectilem

    … and not to get friends, the best and finest furniture of life, so to speakCic. Amic. 55

    In the entry for get

  • in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē. ibi ut sint omnia parāta

    We expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. See that everything is ready there.Cic. Fam. 14.20.1

    In the entry for prepare

  • Quandō vīs venī, parāta rēs erit. — Properā modo.

    Come whenever you like: it’ll be ready. — Just hurry.Plaut. Men. 215

    In the entry for prepare

  • Aesōpus dominō sōlus cum esset familia, parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius.

    Aesop, the only slave his master had, was told to get dinner ready earlier than usual.Phaedr. 3.19.1–2
